messages:
Maya Patel: Quick heads-up — during today's onboarding sync Kestrel reported higher-than-expected latency and token spend. p95 ~880ms, avg tokens per call ~420, cost/token ~ $0.0009. Thinking we should propose a compact-model fallback + split routing to reduce cost while preserving tail latency. Anyone see immediate blockers?
Ibrahim Khan: +1 to compact fallback. Their workload is very prefix-heavy, so prefix/KV caching + switching to a q4_0 or int8 compact variant should help. I ran a quick sim: q4_0 model (rwd/opt-7b-q4) gave ~40% token cost reduction in our bench. :chart_with_downwards_trend:
Jules Park: FYI infra note: some of their Dedicated nodes are older A10s — int8 kernel perf is okay but we need to ensure fused kernels are available in the runtime build. If we route to a variant that requires different kernels, we should add a compatibility check in the rollout.
Priya R: Good call. From CS side I want a short canary plan we can present to the customer — minimize user-facing risk. Proposal: 1) 2% traffic -> compact fallback + cache for 24h, 2) monitor latency & quality (prompt set) for 48h, 3) increase to 25% if no regressions. I'll own comms.
Ibrahim Khan: Sounds right. Suggest routing rule like: ```route { match: prefix; weight: 98@rwd/opt-13b; weight: 2@rwd/opt-7b-q4 }``` and enable `prefix_cache: true` for that customer. We'll need to enable kv cache warmup to avoid cold-start p95 spikes.
Jules Park: Also add a runtime check: `rlctl model-check --model rwd/opt-7b-q4 --node-group kestrel-prod` before canary. If any node lacks kernel support, fail safe and pin to fallback CPU(less ideal) or use hosted pool.
Priya R: I'll prepare the customer-facing playbook: expected cost delta 35-50%, expected p95 change: -50ms on average after cache warms. Will also include rollback wording and a small eval checklist (edge prompts to verify hallucination/regression).
Maya Patel: Can someone add a short snippet we can paste into their onboarding ticket with the config & timeline? Keep it short so Solutions Eng can copy into the support ticket.
Ibrahim Khan: Pasting quick snippet (for ticket): ```# Canary config for Kestrel
canary: true
traffic_split:
  - model: rwd/opt-13b
    weight: 98
  - model: rwd/opt-7b-q4
    weight: 2
prefix_cache: true
kv_warmup: true
monitoring: [latency.p95, tokens_per_call, custom_prompt_eval]
rollback_if: latency.p95 > baseline*1.3 OR eval_regression > 2%```
Priya R: I'll post that and schedule a short call with Kestrel's engineering lead for tomorrow 11am PT. Also asking them for 10 representative prompts we can use for eval.
deploy-bot: scheduled canary deployment for customer=kestrel at 2028-04-02T11:00:00Z (can be cancelled).
Maya Patel: :thumbsup: thanks team. Jules — can you run the `model-check` before the call and update this thread with results? If green we'll proceed with canary at the scheduled time.
Jules Park: Running `rlctl model-check` now, will paste results in a min.
ops-bot: reminder: add `kestrel-canary` to the retention/observability dashboard so CS can see token breakdowns and p95 traces.
Jules Park: model-check output: all nodes in kestrel-prod group report q4 kernel v2.3.1 available. No compile failures. Ready for canary. :white_check_mark:
Priya R: Great — I'll confirm with the customer and post the eval checklist into the ticket. Also flagging this as a renewal risk mitigation in our CRM (Kestrel renewal Q3).
Maya Patel: Perfect. After 48h of canary let's regroup here with metrics + a short note on quality from their prompts. If all good, Ops please prepare a 25% ramp plan.
Ibrahim Khan: I'll prepare a short runbook for rollback steps (force route back to rwd/opt-13b, disable prefix_cache if needed). Posting it to the ticket as well.
Maya Patel: Thanks everyone — nice quick cross-team sync.
